Triage (first-touch grading, 2026-08-21): `finding` → `pm:blocked`, type Task. The body already carries the machine-readable `Blocked-by: #5564` line and the card is correct that the cleanup is only safe after that fix lands — removing a refetch-loop guard while the memo is still unstable would reintroduce the loop it guards. The unlock scan will return this to the queue when #5564 closes; on return, re-verify on the merged ref that PR #5585's memo stabilisation actually landed on both paths, then queue with the card's own test requirement (fetch-count pin across re-renders, inside and outside a provider).

Second item noted on the card (`ObjectTimeline`'s third hand-rolled wrapper duplicating `useSafeFieldLabel`) is a separate question — on unlock, the returning triage pass should decide whether it gets its own card rather than letting it ride silently.

_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

Unlock (same triage round, minutes after the block was placed): #5564 closed during this round — fix PR #5585 is on `origin/main` (`38a9568`, "hold useObjectLabel's memo when no i18next instance is bound"), which is exactly the condition this card's `Blocked-by: #5564` waited for. Both release checks pass (the blocked-transition comment above is the latest condition on this card; no newer merged PR landed on the card after it). `pm:blocked` → `pm:queue`.

Claim-time requirements stand as written in the grading comment: verify the memo holds on both paths on the merged ref, then remove the ref indirection with a fetch-count pin across re-renders inside and outside a provider. Size/model suggestion: S–M. The `ObjectTimeline` third-wrapper question noted on the card still wants its own card decision from whoever implements this.

Per the triage note it wants its own card decision — the dev files it as a fresh card and links it back to this one rather than answering it inside this PR.
